subject: radiology
title: Pulmonary embolism and venous de-bulking

steps.tx: A large pulmonary embolus strains the right heart quickly, so reperfusion urgency follows blood pressure and strain. **Massive pulmonary embolism** with shock and pressor need demands instant reperfusion beyond heparin alone for survival. **Submassive embolism** with right heart strain but stable pressure earns monitored care with escalation ready nearby. **Catheter directed therapy** delivers lytic drug into the pulmonary trunk, with ultrasound assistance that loosens clot locally. **Systemic lysis** suits arrest and collapse when a catheter route would take too long to save life.
steps.say: A large pulmonary embolus strains the right heart quickly so reperfusion urgency follows pressure and strain. Massive embolism with shock is an emergency and it demands instant reperfusion beyond heparin alone. Submassive embolism with heart strain but stable pressure earns monitored care with escalation ready. Catheter therapy delivers lytic drug into the pulmonary trunk with ultrasound assistance that loosens clot. Systemic lysis suits arrest and collapse when a catheter route would take too long.

steps.tx: This chest CT shows a **saddle embolus** that straddles the bifurcation of the main pulmonary trunk in the centre. The upper inset compares ventricular size and shows **right heart strain**, where the right ventricle enlarges and the septum bows leftward. The lower inset shows a **catheter directed lytic catheter** already positioned for local treatment in the pulmonary artery. The image matters for the exam because clot position plus strain separates massive and submassive disease. That separation then decides between systemic lysis, catheter therapy and anticoagulation alone.

steps.tx: Leg clot threatens the lung, and massive iliofemoral clot also threatens the leg itself in phlegmasia. **Phlegmasia with a threatened limb** from massive iliofemoral clot needs urgent de bulking to save tissue. **Pharmacomechanical thrombectomy** macerates clot with aspiration plus lytic drug and clears the vein faster than anticoagulation alone. A **May Thurner compression** behind cleared clot needs a stent so the vein stays open afterwards. An IVC procedure pairs a filter with clot removal when travelling emboli threaten the lungs repeatedly.
steps.say: Leg clot threatens the lung and massive iliofemoral clot also threatens the leg itself in phlegmasia. A threatened limb from massive iliofemoral clot needs urgent de bulking to save tissue quickly. Mechanical maceration with aspiration plus lytic drug is faster and it clears the vein than anticoagulation alone. A venous compression behind cleared clot needs a stent so the vein stays open. A caval procedure pairs a filter with clot removal when travelling emboli threaten lungs.

steps.tx: Lytic treatment in pulmonary embolism still respects the brain and the abdomen, where bleeding causes catastrophe. **Absolute contraindications** mirror limb rules and include a recent brain bleed and recent neurosurgery in that patient. A collapsing mother in **pregnancy** needs individual judgement, because maternal death outweighs fetal lytic risk in extremis. The postoperative window weighs days since surgery against dying lungs when the team considers any lytic dose. A **half dose catheter regimen** trims bleeding when a full systemic dose threatens the patient excessively.
steps.say: Lytic treatment in pulmonary embolism still respects the brain and the abdomen where bleeding causes catastrophe. Absolute bans mirror limb rules and include a recent brain bleed and recent neurosurgery. A collapsing mother in pregnancy needs individual judgement because maternal death outweighs fetal risk greatly. The postoperative window weighs days since surgery against dying lungs during team deliberation. A reduced catheter dose trims bleeding when a full systemic dose threatens the patient.

steps.tx: Right heart recovery takes time after reperfusion, so monitoring continues well beyond the lytic infusion itself. **Echo with troponin** tracks right heart recovery carefully and shows whether strain resolves or persists afterwards. **Anticoagulation** continues once lytic treatment stops, because continued treatment prevents early re clotting in the lungs. A **retrievable filter** leaves the cava once drugs resume and the trap holds no significant clot. An unprovoked clot prompts thrombophilia and cancer screening because the cause shapes lifelong treatment decisions.
